<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="BRPXQZME" />{{running header|{{smaller|{{asc|ODE 10.}}}}|{{asc|THE MAJOR ODES OF THE KINGDOM.}}|395}}{{rule}}</noinclude><ref follow="p394_2">removed to it, simply making the necessary repairs and alterations. This explains how we find nothing about the divinations which should have preceded so important a step as the founding of a new capital.</ref>He repaired the walls along the (old) moat.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
His establishing himself in Făng was according to (the pattern of his forefathers),{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
It was not that he was in haste to gratify his wishes;—{{lb}}It
was to show the filial duty that had come down to him.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
A sovereign true was the royal prince!

His royal merit was brightly displayed{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
By those walls of Făng.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
There were collected (the sympathies of the people of) the four quarters,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Who regarded the royal prince as their protector.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
A sovereign true was the royal prince!

The Făng-water flowed on to the east (of the city),{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Through the meritorious labour of {{tooltip|Yü|Yǔ}}.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
There were collected (the sympathies of the people of) the four quarters,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Who would have the great king as their ruler.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
A sovereign true was the great king<ref>The writer has passed on to [[w:King Wu of Zhou|Wû]], who did actually become king.</ref>!

{{anchor|st6}}In the capital of {{tooltip|Hâo|Hào}} he built his hall with its circlet of water<ref>See on [[Sacred Books of the East/Volume 3/The Shih/Odes of the Temple and the Altar/The Praise Odes of Lû/Ode 3#circlet_of_water|the third of the Praise Odes of Lû in Part IV]].</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
From the west to the east,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
From the south to the north,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
There was not a thought but did him homage.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
A sovereign true was the great king!

{{anchor|st7}}He examined and divined, did the king,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
About settling in the capital of Hâo.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The tortoise-shell decided the site<ref>[[w:Haojing|Hâo]] was built by [[w:King Wu of Zhou|Wû]], and hence we have the account of his divining about the site and the undertaking.</ref>,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And king {{tooltip|Wû|Wǔ}} completed the city.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
A sovereign true was king Wû!
